standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a system of parameters extending a given element avoiding the minimal primes
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the g_1, ..., g_{d-1} that the perturbation argument needs.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a Noetherian ring a power of the radical of an ideal lies in the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the exponent n from which N = n + 1 is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relation 1 + a is a unit when a lies in the maximal ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes the first ideal generator absorb the perturbation without changing the ideal.

core_obligations: Use the existence lemma to find g_1, ..., g_{d-1} in m such that f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is a system of parameters for R, so that m = sqrt((f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1})) (proof lines 38363-38366).
By the Noetherian power lemma choose n with m^n contained in (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}), and claim that N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38367-38369).
For h in m^N use the choice of N to write h = a f + sum b_i g_i with a and b_i in m (proof lines 38370-38371).
Compute the displayed chain of equalities (f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = ((1 + a) f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}), using that 1 + a is a unit of R (proof lines 38372-38381).
Conclude both that f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is a system of parameters and that the two length quotients are equal (proof lines 38381-38383).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (R, m) of dimension d and an element f in m contained in no minimal prime of R, and asserts the existence of g_1, ..., g_{d-1} in m and an integer N such that f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is a system of parameters and such that for every h in m^N the sequence f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} is again a system of parameters with the same length quotient (source lines 38347-38360). The proof is an explicit computation. By the preceding existence lemma there are g_1, ..., g_{d-1} making f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1} a system of parameters, so that m = sqrt((f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1})); by the Noetherian power lemma there is n with m^n contained in (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}), and the proof claims N = n + 1 works (proof lines 38363-38369). The verification is a direct ideal computation: for h in m^N one writes h = a f + sum b_i g_i with a, b_i in m, and then the displayed chain of equalities shows that (f + h, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = ((1 + a) f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) = (f, g_1, ..., g_{d-1}) because 1 + a is a unit of R, which gives both the system-of-parameters claim and the equality of lengths (proof lines 38370-38383). The non-routine content is the choice N = n + 1 that makes the perturbation absorbable into the first ideal generator.
